title: Creating a new branch: Firecrawl comes to Toronto
summary: We're opening our first office outside San Francisco in downtown Toronto, home of our new Ontario subsidiary and a full engineering and product team.
body_markdown:
Today we're opening our Toronto office. It's our first outside San Francisco, it's downtown in the Entertainment District, and it's the home of our new Ontario subsidiary. I want to explain why this matters to us, because it's bigger than a new address.


We started Firecrawl to give AI agents access to the world's knowledge. For a long time, most people knew us as the company that makes it really easy to scrape the web. Our head of brand likes to say we had to scrape, then crawl, then run. Where we're running is knowledge.


More than 1.5 million people build with Firecrawl today. In September we[launched Alexandria](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/introducing-alexandria-series-b) , our knowledge infrastructure for AI agents, and raised a $75 million Series B led by Smash Capital. Toronto is the next step.


## Why we built Alexandria


Agents are doing real work now. They research companies, review scientific literature and write production code. And they're only as good as what they can learn.


The open web gets them part of the way. But much of the most valuable knowledge, from company and people data to financial and scientific records, sits behind paywalls and private APIs, each with its own integration, pricing and format. Alexandria gives agents one place to reach all of it: 88 data providers so far, our own Research, Developer and Government Indexes, and the live web. That's more than 113 million indexed sources, and it grows every week.


In practice, that means an agent can pull every open job posting for a role, look up a doctor in a public health registry or compare a package across registries, without anyone wiring up a new integration for each one. In our internal evals, agents using Alexandria scored 21% higher on answer quality than agents using built-in web tools.


## Why this matters


Superintelligence will need more knowledge than any system before it. Where that knowledge comes from, and whether it's true, is one of the most important problems being worked on right now.


We also believe the people who share knowledge should get something for it. That's why we pay providers when agents use their data. AI is creating a new knowledge economy, one where people get paid for knowledge worth sharing and agents use it to create knowledge worth knowing. Alexandria is the economic model that makes that possible.


## Why Toronto


Toronto has been at the heart of modern AI from the start. So much of the research the whole field builds on came out of this city, and it's still full of people pushing the frontier forward. If you're building knowledge infrastructure for AI agents, this is where you want to be.


Mayor Olivia Chow put it well: "Companies like Firecrawl choose Toronto because of our talent, our universities, and our diversity." That's exactly what drew us here, and we're proud to bring good jobs with us.


## What the Toronto team will build


Toronto is a full engineering and product office. The team here will expand Alexandria's indexes, bring more data providers onto the platform and support Canada's fast-growing community of developers building AI agents.


We're also working with Toronto Global, the investment attraction agency for the Toronto Region, to connect with local universities and the region's tech community. If you run a meetup, a lab or a student group, we'd love to meet you.


## Come build with us


We're hiring for 14 roles in Toronto across engineering, research and growth. The people who join now will shape what Alexandria becomes, and it's really fun to build on the frontier. Every open role is at[firecrawl.dev/careers](https://www.firecrawl.dev/careers) .


If you're in Toronto, come say hi. We're so happy to be here.
